question: Assume today is 2026-09-14. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of visitor arrivals to Hong Kong in September 2026, as it will be first reported (provisional figure) in the Hong Kong Tourism Board's monthly visitor arrivals press release.

target.what: Total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong (all source markets, worldwide, arrivals counted at immigration/entry, i.e. visitor trips not unique persons) during calendar September 2026, as first reported provisionally by the Hong Kong Tourism Board in its monthly visitor arrivals press release
target.cadence: monthly press release, typically published mid-to-late in the following month (provisional figures)
target.caveats: Target period is future/ongoing relative to the 2026-09-14 cutoff, so no September 2026 data exist; must be forecast. Definition is visitor arrivals (trips), not unique visitors; includes same-day and overnight, all nationalities, land/sea/air. Excludes Hong Kong residents returning. Provisional fig

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 arrivals ≈ September 2025 arrivals × (recent YoY growth trend). September is seasonally lower than summer peak; own history gives level and seasonality.
candidates.data_to_find: HKTB monthly total visitor arrivals for Sep 2023, Sep 2024, Sep 2025 and the most recent months published before 2026-09-14 (e.g. Jan–Jul 2026), plus YoY growth rates.
search_hints: 旅発局 訪港旅客 統計 2026

candidates.perspective: Immigration Department / airport and land boundary throughput
candidates.hypothesis: Total arrivals ≈ sum of air, land, sea arrivals; airport passenger and land-crossing (Lo Wu, Lok Ma Chau, HZMB) daily counts constrain the total and give a cross-check.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly/daily passenger throughput at HKIA, land boundary control points, and high-speed rail for recent months and September 2025; conversion from passenger counts to visitor arrivals.
search_hints: Hong Kong International Airport passenger traffic monthly 2026
immigration department daily arrivals statistics Hong Kong

candidates.hypothesis: Total = mainland arrivals + short-haul + long-haul; mainland dominates (~75%). Mainland outbound travel and Shenzhen border crossing data constrain the largest component.
candidates.data_to_find: Mainland visitor arrivals to HK recent months and Sep 2025; mainland outbound trip volumes; Shenzhen-HK crossing volumes.
search_hints: 内地访港旅客 2026 统计

candidates.data_to_find: HK hotel room supply, occupancy rate, average length of stay, and overnight visitor share for recent months and Sep 2025.
search_hints: Hong Kong overnight visitors average length of stay 2026

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 has no major holiday (Mid-Autumn timing varies); typhoon season and any visa/policy changes shift arrivals. Adjust trend for calendar and event effects.

assumptions.name: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025
assumptions.rationale: Q1 2026 arrivals grew +17% YoY (p35) and Jan–May 2026 reached ~23m (p37), indicating strong but decelerating growth from the +8% seen in September 2025 (p3). September is a seasonally softer month with no major holiday, so growth likely moderates below the Q1 pace; central 12% with wide band reflecting deceleration and typhoon/visa uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 growth continues the 2026 trend but decelerates from Q1's +17% toward high-single/low-double digits.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp 2026 slowdown (e.g. monthly 2026 arrivals growth falling below ~5%) or a major disruption (typhoon, policy) in September 2026.

assumptions.name: September seasonal factor relative to annual average
assumptions.rationale: September is a below-peak month; using the September 2025 share of the Jan–Sep 2025 cumulative (p1/p9 ≈ 0.090) adjusted down slightly for the absence of summer peak, gives roughly 1/12 with a modest seasonal discount. Used only if apportioning an annual figure.
assumptions.applies_when: Apportioning a full-year 2026 forecast to September.
assumptions.falsified_by: Monthly seasonal data showing September share materially different from ~8–9% of annual.

assumptions.name: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025

assumptions.name: September 2026 level relative to the Jan–May 2026 monthly average

assumptions.applies_when: Scaling the Jan–May 2026 monthly average run-rate to a September 2026 monthly level.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a strong September-specific event (major festival, policy change, or typhoon disruption) pushing September well above or below the average month.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
